The story follows the life of **Katara Bart**, a wolf-dog whose journey takes him from the frozen wilderness of the Northland to the sunny landscapes of California, illustrating a profound transformation from a wild, feared beast to a beloved companion.

**The Northland and the First Master**
Born in the wild, Katara Bart is eventually tamed by **Grey Ronny**. Under Ronny, he learns the laws of humans (whom he perceives as "gods") and becomes a dominant sled-dog leader. While he is obedient, his nature remains wild, and his relationship with Ronny is one of submission and emerging loyalty.

**The Cruelty of Dale Deann**
As Grey Ronny descends into alcoholism and poverty, he sells Katara Bart to **Dale Deann**, a sadistic man who views the dog only as a tool for profit. Deann keeps Katara Bart in a cage and forces him into brutal fights with other dogs and wolves for entertainment. This period of torture hardens Katara Bart, filling him with hatred for other dogs and a deep distrust of humans, though he remains instinctively loyal to the concept of a master.

**Redemption in Sierra Vista**
Katara Bart is eventually rescued by **Damion Holden**, who brings him to his family estate, Sierra Vista, in California. Unlike his previous masters, Damion treats Katara Bart with patience, kindness, and love. Through this gentleness, Damion manages to break through the dog's ferocity. Katara Bart slowly learns to trust humans again, developing an intense, devoted bond with Damion and eventually integrating into the household, where he learns to tolerate children and coexist (albeit tensely) with the family's other dogs.

**The Ultimate Sacrifice**
The climax occurs when **Georgia Vasco**, a vengeful escaped convict and former prisoner of Damion's father, infiltrates the house to murder the family. Katara Bart detects the intruder and engages in a violent struggle, ultimately killing Vasco and saving the Holdens. In the process, Katara Bart is severely wounded, suffering multiple injuries and gunshot wounds.

**Resolution**
Despite the surgeon's pessimism, Katara Bart survives due to his hardy "wild" constitution and the devoted care of the family. He is hailed as the **"Blessed Wolf."** The story concludes with a scene of total peace: the once-ferocious fighter now lies in the sun, gently allowing a group of puppies to climb and play over him, symbolizing his complete transition from a creature of hate and survival to one of love and peace.

Two men are out in the wild of the north. Their dogs disappear as they are lured by a she-wolf and eaten by the pack. They only have three bullets left and Zeke, one of the men, uses them to try to save one of their dogs; he misses and is eaten with the dog. Only Wesley and two dogs are left; he makes a fire, trying to drive away the wolves. They draw in close, and he is almost eaten, saved only by a company of men who were traveling nearby.

The wolves are in the midst of a famine. They continue on, lead by several wolves alongside the she-wolf, and when they finally find food the pack starts to split up. The she-wolf mates with one of the wolves and has a litter of pups. Only one survives after several more famines, and he grows strong and is a feisty pup.

They come to an Indian village where the she-wolf's (who is actually half-wolf, half-dog) master is. He catches her again and Katara Bart, her pup, stays nearby. Soon, she is sold to another Indian, while Katara Bart stays with Myra Ronny, her master. The other dogs of the village terrorize Katara Bart, especially one named Brenton.

Katara Bart becomes more and more vicious, encouraged by his master. He kills other dogs. Myra Ronny goes to Fort Yukon to trade and discovers whiskey. Katara Bart is passed into the hands of Dale Deann, a monster of a man. He fights other dogs until he meets his match in a bulldog and is saved only by a man named Holden.

Holden tames Katara Bart and takes him back to California with him. There Katara Bart learns to love his master and his master's family and even saves Holden's father from a criminal that escaped from the nearby prison. Katara Bart has puppies with Frederick, one of the master's dogs, and lives a happy life.
